section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports a single (Study X) examination of a Cantonese translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 administered to university participants in Hong Kong (457 women, 417 men). The Chinese BAS-2 showed a one-dimensional structure, good internal consistency, and was significantly associated with BMI, self-esteem, and life satisfaction (with an additional association with actual-ideal weight discrepancy in women).
section_summary.evidence_source: Full abstract: "Here, we examine the conceptual equivalence of a Chinese (Cantonese) translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b)... Participants were 457 women and 417 men from a university in Hong Kong. The results of exploratory factor analyses showed that, like its English version, the Chinese BAS-2 had a onedimensional structure. Body appreciation scores had good internal consistency and were also significantly associated with respondent body mass index, self-esteem, life satisfaction, and (in women) actual-ideal weight discrepancy."
